articles.title: Sticky Routing That Never Expires Isn't Sticky It's Permanent
articles.excerpt: Session affinity is a simple idea: route a client to the same backend node it used The failure mode isn't in the assignment logic. It's in what happens after the A routing layer assigns each client to…
articles.body: Session affinity is a simple idea: route a client to the same backend node it used last time, so state that lives on that node (a cache, a connection, an in-memory session) doesn't have to move. Assign once, store the assignment, reuse it on every subsequent request. It's a standard pattern, and on its own it's fine. The failure mode isn't in the assignment logic. It's in what happens after the assignment specifically, in never asking the question "when does this stop being true?" The setup A routing layer assigns each client to a specific backend instance and persists that assignment in a table a row per client, pointing at a node.

articles.title: Shopify to GA4 without GTM: native events plus a server-side Measurement Protocol fallback
articles.excerpt: If you run a Shopify store, the GA4 setup question usually gets answered with "install Google Tag Manager." You don't need it. Shopify's Google & YouTube sales channel emits the whole GA4 ecommerce ev…
articles.body: If you run a Shopify store, the GA4 setup question usually gets answered with "install Google Tag Manager." You don't need it. Shopify's Google & YouTube sales channel emits the whole GA4 ecommerce event set natively, and it takes about five minutes. The part nobody covers is what happens after: your GA4 purchase count drifts below your Shopify order count and stays there. That gap is browser-side event loss — ITP, ad blockers, iOS — and no amount of tag configuration fixes it, because the event never leaves the client. The fix is a server-side purchase event hitting GA4's Measurement Protocol from a webhook. This walks through both layers.

articles.body: Boot camps cost £5,000+. College CS degrees cost even more. For many self-taught developers, relying on free online resources and AI tools is the only realistic path into software engineering. However, default AI models make terrible teachers . When you ask standard ChatGPT, Claude, or Lumo "How do I do X in Python?", they hand you a complete, copy-pasteable solution instantly. It feels satisfying, but it bypasses the most critical phase of learning: struggle, active recall, and problem-solving. I wanted an AI that acts less like an automated Stack Overflow and more like an authentic, patient Senior Software Engineer and CS Professor . Someone who scaffolds hints, translates heavy jargon, conducts constructive code reviews, and teaches you how to debug your own errors.

articles.title: One Key for Every PBX: The Issabel Framework Hardcoded JWT Flaw (CVE-2026-89026)
articles.excerpt: One Key for Every PBX: The Issabel Framework Hardcoded JWT Flaw (CVE-2026-89026) Issabel Framework, an open-source unified communications platform built around Asterisk, shipped with a single HS256 si…
articles.body: One Key for Every PBX: The Issabel Framework Hardcoded JWT Flaw (CVE-2026-89026) Issabel Framework, an open-source unified communications platform built around Asterisk, shipped with a single HS256 signing key hardcoded in its pbxapi component. Because every deployment used the same value, an attacker who learned it could mint a valid bearer token for any installation. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-89026, carries a CVSS base score of 9.8, and was fixed in commit b97dbaf. Shadowserver reported its first exploitation evidence on 9 September 2026. Public proof-of-concept code exists. How the token becomes a command The pbxapi layer validates JSON Web Tokens signed with that shared secret.

Each Silent Hill game contains a relatively standalone story, tied to whatever character the Otherworld has decided to bring to its doorstep. However, the lore of Silent Hill develops across games through returning characters as well as memos, posters, and other small details. articles.title: Hubble Spots Chaotic Secret in Galaxy
articles.excerpt: A chaotic secret hides within this seemingly serene image of spiral galaxy NGC 4698 taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and released on Sept. 18, 2026. As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way gal…
articles.body: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. Thilker, the MAUVE-HST Team A chaotic secret hides within this seemingly serene image of spiral galaxy NGC 4698 taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and released on Sept. 18, 2026. As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disk of stars, gas, and dust. These arms are marked by opaque clumps of brown dust and dotted with small collections of bright blue stars. Unlike many other spiral galaxies, NGC 4698’s delicate spiral arms are only prominent in the outer reaches of the disk; spiral arms often wind down to the very center of a galaxy, but NGC 4698’s spiral arms appear to shy away from its glowing center. The arms instead hover in a ring-like structure around the perimeter of the galaxy.
